newsitem.title: PERU: Ex U.N. head to take Peru phonetap charges to OAS. [CORRECTED 13:52 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Ex U.N. head to take Peru phonetap charges to OAS. [CORRECTED 13:52 GMT]

text.p: Former United Nations head Javier Perez de Cuellar will take charges that Peru's security forces tapped his telephones during the 1995 presidential campaign to an international human rights body, his lawyer said on Sunday.

Carlos Chipoco said his client would take the case this week to the Interamerican Human Rights Commission of the Organisation of American States (OAS) in Washington because he did not think a local investigation would be impartial (deletes extraneous "not").
"We believe that in this country Peruvians' rights are not respected and so we have decided to go to the OAS commission because it is an impartial body," Chipoco told Reuters.
Perez de Cuellar alleges the National Intelligence Service listened in on his conversations during the 1995 campaign, which he lost to President Alberto Fujimori.

The former U.N. chief, who is leader of Peru's main opposition party, is the most high-profile target in a telephone espionage scandal that has damaged Fujimori's popularity. A local TV station alleged that security forces bugged the phones of up to 150 journalists and politicians.

Despite the fact the government ordered a special public prosecutor to investigate the scandal, Peru's Congress decided to hold its own inquiry into the allegations. Opposition legislators complained the investigator was hand-picked by the government and pushed for a Congress-based inquiry.
